Class TypeHierarchyWriter

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.inject.writer.TypeHierarchyWriter
@Internal public final class TypeHierarchyWriter extends Object
Writes the record of the generic hierarchy of a type, a TypeHierarchy found at run time with TypeHierarchies. See VisitorContext.recordTypeHierarchy(ClassElement, Element...).

A record is a class with a constructor and nothing else, which passes the type, its variables, its direct super types and all its super types, built with the argument factories from class constants, to GeneratedTypeHierarchy. It is marked Generated, so that the visitors of a compiler that hands the classes written in a round to the next one, as javac does, do not take it for a class of the application, and a record is never itself recorded. It is named after the top-level class of the first originating element, which owns it and its service entry, and written into the package of that element; only a type that is itself not public is recorded in its own package, the one package that can name it. A super type that the record cannot name, a class that is not public and of another package than the record or one whose arguments name such a class, is left out of the recorded closure with the types above it kept, and is recorded by the name of its class instead (TypeHierarchy.getOmittedSuperTypeNames()), and the names are reported to the caller as well; a type whose variables are bounded by such a class is refused.

  • Method Details

    • write

      public static TypeHierarchyRecord write(ClassElement type, VisitorContext context, Element... originatingElements)
      Writes the record of a type, and reports what it says and leaves out. A type recorded several times from the same top-level class is written once: a compiler that refuses a second write of the same class is taken at its word. A type recorded from several classes is written for each, see TypeHierarchies.find(String, ClassLoader).
      Parameters:
      type - The type, a declaration
      context - The visitor context
      originatingElements - The originating elements, at least one
      Returns:
      The record
      Throws:
      ProcessingException - if no record can describe the type, or the record cannot be written

    • writeIfRecordable

      public static Optional<TypeHierarchyRecord> writeIfRecordable(ClassElement type, VisitorContext context, Element... originatingElements)
      Writes the record of a type as write(ClassElement, VisitorContext, Element...) does, unless no record can describe the type, which is then not written.
      Parameters:
      type - The type, a declaration
      context - The visitor context
      originatingElements - The originating elements, at least one
      Returns:
      The record, or empty when no record can describe the type
      Throws:
      ProcessingException - if the record cannot be written
